correctness.rationale: For each support, a cycle, a within-tree forced comparability, or a directed quotient cycle explicitly supplies an unextendable orientation. Conversely every orientation of a forest with antichain components and an acyclic quotient produces an acyclic union with the precedence relation, hence a linear extension. Longest-chain vertices occupy distinct components for an n-h upper bound, and rank-level spanning trees attain it. All edge cases include n=0. A separate direct trace engine agrees on 90,975 support cases across all posets through four elements and 75 five-element posets.

value.rationale: The all-poset theorem classifies every shattered pair-query support, including a genuinely nonlocal quotient-cycle obstruction, and collapses the maximal VC dimension to n minus longest-chain length. This creates a tractable structural learning invariant even for height-two posets where counting compatible total orders is #P-hard. The full shattering complex provides practical support selection information beyond a scalar dimension.
